subject: Marketplace SKU attribution: partner-managed usage & co-sell ops
message_1_headers:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <partnership@cloudforge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace SKU attribution: partner-managed usage & co-sell ops
message_1_body:
Alex —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We took notes on the partner-managed SKU flow you described and sketched a proposed metering map (attached) that should meet Marketplace requirements while preserving attribution back to CloudForge for co-sell credit. High-level items in the attachment:

- Metering dimension to use: partner_instance_id + sku_token
- Entitlement check: call Redwood entitlement API for mapping to customer account
- Usage reporting: daily batched CSV push to marketplace ingestion endpoint (with a near-real-time fallback for large customers)

Questions we need to resolve before we lock the listing:
1) Billing flow: do you want usage billed through CloudForge (reseller flow) or billed direct to customer with partner crediting?
2) Metering latency tolerance: does your billing reconciliation tolerate 24h delay, or do you need sub-1h near-real-time for high-volume SKUs?
3) Who will own the SKU metadata in the marketplace catalog (CloudForge or Redwood) — this determines who updates pricing/terms in the catalog UI.

Ben/Olga — looping you both in to surface any coms or technical blockers you see.

Next steps I propose:
- CloudForge confirms billing choice and latency need (this week)
- Redwood infra/marketplace team (Vivek) reviews integration checklist and flags infra changes (by EOD Tue)
- Draft a short mutual action plan and evidence list for AWS/GCP listing submission (Ben to own the MAP)

I've attached the proposed-metering-map.xlsx — it's intentionally conservative on attribution tags; we can add extra telemetry if CloudForge needs it.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Diego.mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: proposed-metering-map.xlsx (workbook, 3 sheets: mapping, examples, reconciliation-guidance)
message_2_headers:
From: Alex Mercer <partnership@cloudforge.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@amazon.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU attribution: partner-managed usage & co-sell ops
message_2_body:
Diego —

Appreciate the clear note and the spreadsheet. Quick answers up front:
1) We prefer reseller-billing (CloudForge invoices customers, AWS/GCP treats CloudForge as the publisher/reseller). That keeps our sales motions intact and simplifies incentives.
2) Metering latency: 6–12 hours is fine for 90% of customers, but we need a near-real-time path (sub-30m) for any enterprise customers we flag as 'fast-billing' in the MAP.
3) CloudForge will own SKU metadata and pricing, but we need Redwood to be able to pull updates (read-only) so the listing UI stays consistent.

Priya — adding you to ensure the proposed mapping aligns with the AWS co-sell tagging approach (we'll need the partner resource ARNs and co-sell tags to flow into attribution).

A couple of implementation asks from our side:
- Can Redwood expose a webhook that confirms ingestion of daily reports? We want confirmation for our reconciliation.
- Are there sample payloads for the near-real-time fallback? If not, we can coordinate on that next.

We can take the MAP draft and convert it into a short mutual action plan; happy to have my ops lead (cc'd later if needed) take ownership of the reconciliation cadence.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Partnerships | CloudForge
Attachment: none

Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU attribution: partner-managed usage & co-sell ops
message_3_body:
Alex —

That all makes sense and aligns with what I expected. Quick technical notes from our side:

- Webhook: yes — we can spin up a signing-backed webhook endpoint that returns an HTTP 200 on successful ingestion. We'll include an ingestion-id and checksum so you can reconcile batches.
- Near-real-time: we can support an event push (Kafka -> Redact -> marketplace-ingest) pattern. We'll provide a sample JSON payload and a small SDK snippet for CloudForge to produce the event in the format the marketplace expects.

Vivek — tagging you for two asks: 1) confirm if we have any constraints on exposing an ingestion webhook that CloudForge can call (security/ratelimit concerns), and 2) estimate effort to produce the sample payload + 2 small SDK snippets (Node + Python). Can you reply with a short effort estimate and ETA?

Olga/Ben — once Vivek confirms, I'll draft the MAP (1 page) and list required evidence for AWS/GCP submission (service docs, security checklist, metering examples, and test accounts). Ben — can you advise on whether we want PM/SE to join the joint tech call next week for enterprise customers?

Thanks,
Diego

- Sample payload + SDK snippets (Node + Python): small change. We'll produce a 1-page payload spec + two small gists. (Effort: 2 engineer-days, ETA: Sept 22)

Attachments: I uploaded a short draft checklist titled "MVP-integration-checklist.docx" to the shared Drive with the items we'll need for marketplace submission (evidence, test account instructions, required IAM roles). Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/marketplace-co-sell/CF-789

Action items:
1) CloudForge confirms reseller billing and flags any enterprise fast-billing customers (Alex).
2) Diego to draft MAP and circulate (Diego).
3) Vivek to deliver payload spec + SDK snippets by Sept 22 and webhook by Sept 28.
4) Ben/Olga to confirm whether PM/SE join for tech call — please decide by EOD Thu.

If that timeline works for CloudForge, I'll calendar an initial technical onboarding slot for the week of Sept 27.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Manager, Cloud Alliances | Redwood Inference
